finding: M110 (the asymmetric pre/post-news stand-down), which also closes the surviving wording half of M62
course: Saved Ep30 (S3). The episode states TWO stand-down periods of different length, not one: a pre-release block — "you don't open new positions during that window where the news is coming out, like 15 minutes before and after news" — and a separate, longer post-release settle — "after the news came out, you want to wait for the volatility to settle, maybe 30 minutes to 60 minutes after the high impact news comes out. Once the structure start becoming much more clearer, this is where you can continue trading." He also names the values he actually uses for the block — "the default state is probably like 15 minutes, right? But you can set it to 5 minutes, 10 minutes, 30 minutes, 60 minutes" — and, for the block, a floor he recommends rather than imposes: "I would recommend you to at least put it at 15 minutes before and after." The M62 correction stands and is the reason the default is not lowered: the OLD single number (45) already satisfied a 15-minute block and sat inside the 30-60 settle, so the recorded defect was never the number. It was that one knob governed both sides, so a value he sanctions (5/10/15/30) silently collapsed the settle to the same number — 6-12x below his 30-60 — with no warning.
design: `src/news-window.js` (`news-window-v1`) is the owner module and has no dependencies at all: it requires nothing, reads no environment, no filesystem, no path and not even the clock (`now` is passed in), so the rule is a leaf that can be copied out of the tree and answer identically. It carries the episode's own words in `DOCTRINE`, the app's honest boundary in `BASIS` (both numbers are settings and recommendations, the floor is the only refusal, no model and no claim about what a release does to price), the two bounds objects (`news_block_before_min` 1-240 default 15; `news_settle_after_min` 30-240 default 45), `plan()` (clamp on read, with `source` and `clamped` provenance per side), `parse()`/`parsePair()` (request input, refusing rather than coercing), `hit(eventMs, nowMs, plan)` (the ONE asymmetric test: a non-negative offset is judged by the block, a printed release by the settle, boundaries inclusive, NaN/undefined and malformed pairs answer null rather than matching), `detail()` (the note that names the two configured numbers) and `invalid()` (`news_window_invalid`, `news_settle_below_floor`, `news_window_split_required`).

Two account columns, added additively: `news_block_before_min INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 15` and `news_settle_after_min INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 45`, each with its own CHECK including an integer-cast test, plus two additive migrations. The stored CREATE TABLE text is the parent's own text with the two definitions inserted before the closing parenthesis, every pre-existing column keeps its position/type/nullability/default, every inherited fact outside `accounts` and the auth sessions the probe itself creates is byte-identical, and re-opening the database is a no-op.

The engine resolves the pair from the account before the calendar check (the account read moved above it), and `newsCheck` now returns `windows:{before_min, after_min, source, clamped}` with every blocked release carrying its own `side` and `offset_min` — the top-level single `window_min` is gone, not deprecated, and no shipped file or client reads it. The blackout sentence interpolates the account's own two numbers and names the side that caught the release ("in X min" / "printed X min ago"), so the note cannot describe a window the app is not applying. `setup.js`'s fallback states the two windows in the trader's direction instead of a hardcoded one-sided "next 60 minutes" (the surviving M62 half), and the veto carries the blended blackout rather than a second, generic sentence.

Every legacy spelling of the single number is refused with 400 `news_window_split_required` — `window_min`, `windowMin`, `newsWindowMin`, `news_window_min` and `?window=` on the news route, each of them checked BEFORE the split fields so one cannot be smuggled in beside a valid pair and quietly ignored. A settle below 30 is refused with 400 `news_settle_below_floor` on create and on update; a block below the recommended 15 is stored as set with the named warning `news_block_before_below_recommended` and never shortens the settle; a settle longer than the 30-60 he names is stored and reported with `news_settle_outside_stated_range` rather than repaired.

The settings surface is two number fields with their own bounds (1-240 and 30-240), the floor stated in the field note before anything is typed, a fast client-side message for the two refusals, and the two keys always sent together so an unrelated edit such as a rename cannot move either clock.

M111 is NOT solved here and every probe says so in its own words: a calendar that cannot be fetched still reaches this rule as a quiet one (null blackout, no `unavailable` flag, no error on the payload), which is the recorded fail-open. The pair is still echoed on that path so an outage can never be read as "45 minutes was applied and nothing was found", and a failure is not cached the way a success is.
